items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: I've seen Buddy Tate so often you'd think he's home when he's... I saw Lockjaw in Paris, I saw Lockjaw in Denmark, I saw Lockjaw in Sweden... And Sweets Edison and all them guys, [I] see all of them nowadays.

ctx.x: But those two bands, I worked and they both were jazz bands. And the others was commercial. My brother, first thing I worked with my brother before anybody playing alto saxophone and reading music and playing popular numbers and songs from the shows like Shubert's Theater, Shubert's, you know, things like popular numbers for rich people. And we had to play the melody and I was playing little countermelodies and with his trumpet and real soft, muted. That's what I was doing before all of this. Well, that was thing…
Let me ask you about Philadelphia. What other people - Polk and Miller were your main stem - what other jazz and blues people were you associated with during this early period?
